text: This is your night session.
Lights off. Phone face down.
If you've got headphones in, good. The soft tones underneath are built for them.
If you're driving, or anywhere but somewhere you can fall asleep, stop this now and come back later.
Nothing here is magic. It's practice.
For the next few minutes, your brain is going to rehearse the man you already decided to be.
All you have to do is listen.
Let's slow the body down first.
Breathe in through your nose... two... three... four.
And out, slow, through your mouth... two... three... four... five... six.
Again. In... two... three... four.
Out... two... three... four... five... six.
One more. In... two... three... four.
Out... all the way... five... six.
Now keep that rhythm on your own for a few breaths. In for four. Out for six.
Good.
Let the breath go back to whatever it wants to do.
You don't have to do anything right. There's no right way to listen to this.
Thoughts will come. Let them. They're cars on a far-off road. You hear them pass. You don't chase them.
Tonight you're not trying to become anything. You're letting something get practiced.
And you can give yourself permission, right now, to let the day be over.
The calls are done. The texts can wait.
Whatever you said today, and whatever you wish you'd said... it's done.
Tomorrow gets a fresh version of you.
Bring your attention to the top of your head.
Just notice it. You don't have to change anything.
Notice your forehead... and let it go smooth... like a warm hand just passed across it.
Your eyes get heavy behind the lids. The small muscles around them... let go.
Your jaw. You carry a lot there. Every time you held your tongue today, it went into the jaw.
Let your teeth come apart a little. Let your tongue rest.
Your neck softens.
Your shoulders drop... about an inch... and then another inch you didn't know you had.
Feel that weight move down your arms... into your elbows... your forearms... your hands.
Your hands might feel warm. They might feel heavy. Either one is fine.
Your chest rises... and falls... on its own. Nobody's asking it to.
Your stomach. Let it go loose. You don't have to hold anything in for anyone tonight.
Your lower back sinks into the bed.
Your hips. Your thighs. Heavy.
Your knees... your calves... your ankles... all the way down to the soles of your feet.
Your whole body is held now. The bed's got you.
You don't have to hold yourself up. Not tonight.
And with every breath out from here, you can go a little further down ... into rest.
In a moment I'm going to count down from ten to one.
Picture a wide staircase. Ten steps. Warm light. Soft carpet under your feet.
Each number takes you one step down. And each step makes it twice as easy to let go.
Ten. One step down.
Nine. Shoulders loose.
Eight. Deeper... easier.
Seven. Nothing to fix. Nothing to prove.
Six. Halfway down... and twice as relaxed.
...and you can notice how the voices and the music blend together...
Five.
...you don't need to follow every word...
Deeper now.
...part of you listens... and part of you rests...
Four.
...and both parts are learning...
Three. Way down.
...easy...
Two.
...almost there...
And one.
At the bottom of the stairs now. Deeply relaxed.
At the bottom of the stairs there's a door. And on the other side is a quiet room, with a table, and two chairs.
You sit down. And across from you is somebody who has to make a decision.
...you can sit easy...
It might be a buyer. An owner. An investor. Someone interviewing you. It doesn't matter yet.
In the middle of the table there's an old lantern. Brass. Warm.
...steady hands...
And here's the thing about that lantern. Whoever holds it decides where the light goes.
When you talk... and talk... the light swings all over the room. It hits the walls. It hits you. Everybody's looking at you.
...you don't have to fill the room...
But when you ask a question... the light lands on them. On what they want. On what's in their way.
...the light goes where you point it...
And they start to see it. In their own words.
The man holding the lantern doesn't push anybody. He doesn't have to. He points the light... and he waits... while they look.
...ask... and wait...
Sometimes the waiting feels long. That's the part where they're finding it.
...the silence is working...
You've always been able to hold that lantern. Tonight your hands are just getting used to the weight.
...you lead... with questions...
And the more you hold it... the lighter it gets.
...one question at a time...
I lead with questions.
You lead with questions.
The person asking the questions holds the frame.
You hold the frame by asking.
I don't need the perfect line. I need the next question.
You don't need the perfect line. You need the next question.
When I feel pressure, I get curious.
When you feel pressure, you get curious.
I ask... and then I stop talking.
You ask... and then you stop talking.
Silence after a good question isn't awkward. It's working.
The silence is working for you.
I lower the threat before I ask for anything.
You make it safe first.
I never make the next step a test of someone's worth.
You make the next step the obvious move for who they already are.
I let them say it. People believe what they hear themselves say.
You let them say it.
My facts are clean. My edges are human.
Your facts are clean. Your edges are human.
I say the number once, plainly, and then I'm quiet.
You say the number like the weather. Then you're quiet.
I hold the outcome loosely, and the question firmly.
Overthinking is just importance turned up too high. You turn it down, and you ask.
Every conversation gets my questions, even on a bad day.
Wins are normal for you.
I give up talking to go up.
You let them carry the conversation.
One question beats five.
You keep it simple.
I rep it until it breaks. I fix the crack. I rep it again.
That's how you get good.
Short turns. One question. Listen. Reflect one line. Next step.
Short turns. One question. Listen.
I meet people where they are before I try to move them.
You validate first. Then you help.
I give before I ask.
You give first.
One conversation. One lane. One next step.
One next step.
I influence with honest questions. Never tricks.
Honest questions.
If they could read my mind, they'd be fine with what they found.
You'd be fine with them seeing everything.
I'd rather lose a deal than win it with a lie.
A "no" is information. It's not an insult.
Jason... you lead with questions.
Jason... you ask, and you let it land.
Jason... you've got time.
Now let's practice. You're going to see five rooms. In each one, you lead with questions. You don't have to make it perfect. Just watch yourself do it.
You're standing on the lot. Late afternoon. Heat coming up off the asphalt. Keys in your pocket.
A man walks up. His car's been overheating. He's tired, and he's guarded. He's expecting a pitch.
You feel your thumb touch your finger. One breath. And instead of a pitch, you ask.
"What's got you looking?"
And he tells you. You listen. You nod.
"How long's it been doing that?"
"And what's that doing to your week... with work?"
You wait. You let it be quiet. And he says it, in his own words. The write-up from his boss. The tow last month.
You say it back in one line. "So you need something that just starts and goes."
He asks the price. And you say the number once, clean, like it's the weather. Then you ask, "If the numbers make sense, is this the one?"
"Want to drive it now... or after you call your wife?"
He picks one. And you notice how calm you are.
Now you're in a dealer's office. Paper everywhere. A phone buzzing face down on the desk.
The owner leans back. He's heard about AI. He's not impressed.
You don't argue. You don't demo. You start with respect. "Sounds like you've built this on hustle... and it works."
Then you ask. "What happens to a message that comes in at nine at night?"
He laughs a little. Then he stops laughing.
"How many of those go cold in a week, you think?"
"And what's a car worth to you, in gross?"
He does the math out loud. His math. Not yours.
You say the price once, clean. And you stop talking.
The silence stretches. You let it. He says, "Okay. How do we start?"
"After-hours line this week... or Monday?"
Now you're across from an investor. A quiet coffee shop. She's seen a hundred pitches this year.
Your numbers are ready. Exact. Nothing rounded up.
And you don't open with the deck. You open with a question.
"What would make this a clear yes for you?"
She tells you. You listen for the real thing under it.
"What have you seen go wrong in deals like this?"
Then the one that takes nerve. "What worries you most about me... honestly?"
She tells you the truth. And you don't flinch. You thank her. You answer it straight.
You state your terms once. Clean. And you're quiet.
You'd be fine if she walked. And somehow that's exactly why she leans in.
"Data room tonight... and we talk Thursday or Friday?"
Now a conference room. Two buyers across the table. One of them talks. The other one decides.
You feel steady. You ask.
"What made this a priority now?"
"Walk me through how it works today."
"And what's that costing you each month?"
The quiet one finally speaks. You turn your attention to him.
"Who else weighs in on this?"
"Want to bring them on the next call? Tuesday at ten, or Thursday after lunch?"
Last room. An interview. Two people with a list of questions.
They ask you one. And you answer it straight. Clean. Your real numbers. No padding.
Then you hand the light back to them.
"What would make the person in this seat a clear win in the first ninety days?"
They light up a little. They tell you. You listen.
"What's the hardest part of this job that isn't in the posting?"
And near the end, calm, curious... "Is there anything about my background that gives you pause?"
They tell you. You answer it. And you can feel the room shift.
You're not auditioning. You're leading. With questions.
Now let's lock it in.
Gently touch your thumb to your first finger.
Breathe in... and as you breathe out, think one word. Ask.
Feel what's here right now. A calm body. A curious mind. A slow voice.
Let your fingers relax.
Again. Thumb to finger. Breathe in... and out. Ask.
Every time you do this, it gets stronger. Calm body. Curious mind. Next question.
Let go.
One more time. Thumb to finger. Breathe in... and out. Ask.
From now on, any time... any room... eyes open... thumb to finger, one breath... and the next question shows up on its own.
Let your hand rest.
Tomorrow... when someone asks you the price... you say it once, clean... and then you ask a question.
When you feel the urge to explain... you ask instead.
When the silence stretches... you let it.
When they say no... you ask what would have to change... and you let them go easy if nothing would.
...when you feel the urge to explain... you ask...
...when the silence stretches... you let it...
And tonight, while you sleep, your brain does what brains do with practice. It sorts. It keeps what matters.
...it keeps what matters...
You don't have to try to remember any of this. It's already yours.
And now... you can drift.
Nothing left to do.
I lead with questions...
...you hold the light...
...sleep now.
